classification.difficultyReason: Combine equal octagon sides with the right triangles removed from the square.

content.prompt: A carpenter has a square piece of wood of dimensions $1$ metre by $1$ metre. He wants to create a regular octagon by cutting off the corners. What distance $x$ from the edge of the square does the carpenter need to make his cuts?

spec.description: Regular octagon cut from a unit square; original square shown by dashed outlines, without decorative fill.
spec.mathematics: Each removed corner is an isosceles right triangle with legs x. Original height is 1.
spec.answerVisibility: The numerical value of x is not labelled.

answer.short:
$x=\dfrac{2-\sqrt2}{2}\text{ m}$.

Equate the cut side $x\sqrt2$ to the remaining side $1-2x$.
answer.worked:
Each removed corner has perpendicular sides of length $x$. Let its cut edge have length $s$.
$$\begin{align*}s^2&=x^2+x^2\\s&=x\sqrt2.\end{align*}$$
All octagon sides are equal, so
$$\begin{align*}x\sqrt2&=1-2x\\x(2+\sqrt2)&=1\\x&=\frac{1}{2+\sqrt2}\\x&=\frac{2-\sqrt2}{2}\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$
